[quote=cordone;58108898][b]Question of the Day #12:[/b]

[i]What are the major parties, factions, or political rivalries within your nation?[/i][/quote]

The main four parties are:

- The Military Guard: Main goal is to expand the military-industrial complex by annexing as much land as possible, and expanding the naval reach of the ULR. Main supporters are those who are descended from RJR veterans.

- National Progress Party: Main goal is to expand, but at a slow and steady pace, while also modernizing the nation as the world progresses. Most focused on things like international relations, nuclear power, and aid programs. Liked mostly by younger people.

- Governmental Individuality Campaign: Main goal is to keep the nation to itself, only interacting with the world via trade and sometimes military exercises. The least popular party in the ULR, some old people like them.

- Argarino Nativos Derechos (Argos Natives Group): Main goal is preserving native sites with historical significance, obtaining more funds for native towns to help modernize them, as well as nature important to native beliefs. Main supporters are descendants of Native Argos peoples, as well as those who are anti-logging and mining.

[quote=cordone;58108898][b]Question of the Day #12:[/b]

[i]What are the major parties, factions, or political rivalries within your nation?[/i][/quote]
For a young nation, the Anrakan Republic surprisingly has many parties on the political landscape

The current ruling party is the DSAP, or the democratic socialist party

There used to be a big tent party known as the UAP, but had split in recent years
The parties formed from this split were:
1. The LPA - the labor/progressive party
2. The ALP - the liberal party
3. The CAC - the conservative party

There is then finally the ANSP, which is a party made of nationalists and monarchist remnants from the civil war. There are also rumored to be other...authoritarian elements within the party, however the ANSP denies such allegations.

[spoiler]Government Council Meeting of Jan. 3, 2025

There was a tense atmosphere in the room. Government officials commenced small talk with each other as they waited for the meeting to begin. This meeting would mark the cusp of the first year of the current presidents term, as well as the 25th anniversary of the republics founding. So far, the republic has been finally stabilizing, both politically and financially, and is finally in a better position than it has been in years. However, stability can only satisfy people for a period of time. The president had done a fine job continuing the plans put in place by his predecessor, but now was the time for new, bold actions that could define his presidency. That is what this convention of the cabinet is for, ideas for the future.
The sound of the double doors that serve as the entrance to the chamber opening quiet any remaining conversation. Walking through the doors was the President, followed by his closest advisors, the Vice President and the Chief Strategist. Taking their seats at the head of the table, theres a moment of awkward silence as files and reports are pulled out and passed to the head of the table. Once everything is compiled together, the president clears his throat, All right, lets get this meeting underway. So far we have done a great job in recovering from our setbacks. The government has now stabilized for the time being, and the economy is now experiencing an upturn, which is why I believe it is time for us to move forward with more ambitious projects. Before that though, I believe some of you had concerns that you wished to be brought up?

The minister of economics nodded his head before speaking. As you have stated, weve done a good job of bringing the economy into a profitable upturn. Weve also managed to have a mostly self-sufficient economy that has helped our efforts in that regard. However, this economy can only remain in the positive for so long before stagnating. In other words, we need to use this opportunity to expand our efforts to keep our countrys economy growing, and while I know it may upset some of our more, ahem, anti-capitalist members, it may not hurt to extend trade offers to other countries and participate in the global market.

I also agree with this statement, chimes in the minister of foreign affairs. While we have spent these past few years focusing inward for this country, we have neglected our position on the world stage and have little to no interaction with other countries beyond our borders. We are limited in our options though, with a lack of access to the ocean, we have to facilitate trade through neighboring countries. This is why I suggest we focus our efforts in perhaps opening communications with UREV to perhaps-. A scoff from the minister of defense interrupted the foreign ministers train of thought. You cant be serious, UREV?! Those federalists had no issue showing disdain towards the new government when we made the switch to socialist policies. Besides, we've received disturbing reports of expansionist policies and an increased military presence along our borders. Our respectful opinion is that they would much rather subjugate our fair nation rather than offer any sort of cooperation. Surely you must realize that statement is ridiculous? argued the foreign affairs minister. This earned a chuckle from the defense minister, who replied, Ridiculous it may be, but its much better than your naive belief-.

Enough! shouted the Vice President, clearly you both have differing opinions on the matter, but we are wasting time arguing over semantics. The President cleared his throat before interjecting, There may be a possible solution to all your problems. In preparation for this meeting, we had discussed which big project we wished to undertake, and clearly this decision was the right one upon hearing your statements. While the President was talking, the chief strategist got up and grabbed a large roll of paper from the back of the room, unrolling it out on the table to reveal plans of an expansion of the countries borders north and east. What we decided on was to expand our borders to take advantage of the unoccupied space. This expansion would also reach to the coast, where we plan to perhaps set up a naval presence in the area. There are possible expansions planned in the future, but this was what we had planned to move forwards with for the immediate future.

The other ministers looked at the map, some with questioning glances, others with more admirable gazes. The economic minister was the first to speak up. This expedition is rather risky, the cost to maintain this new land would provide a large risk towards financial stability, however with large risks can also mean large rewards. It could also give us naval access that can benefit trade and diplomacy, without forcing ourselves to work through other foreign channels, chimed in the minister of foreign affairs. The defense minister said nothing, but nodded in agreement to the things that were said. Very well, if were all in agreement then we can move forward with this plan, the President said while looking at everyone in the room. Now then, lets take a quick recess while we get the operation prepared.
[/spoiler]
